item.title: Write an update when a supplier breaks a service promise
item.context_text: A company promised that local news subscribers would get a print insert with their delivery. A supplier can print half the copies in time.
item.objective_text: Offer feasible choices without giving some subscribers an unsupported guarantee.
success_conditions: Offer feasible choices without giving some subscribers an unsupported guarantee.

children.title: Read the delivery agreement
children.instructions: Read closely and use the details to answer.
children.prompt_text: Print inserts are included with the Saturday delivery. If the promised insert is unavailable, a subscriber can choose a paper copy by post when ready or request a delivery credit. A PDF can be offered in addition to either choice.

questions.prompt: What alternatives does the agreement leave open?
options: A posted paper copy or a delivery credit
questions.explanation: The two options apply when the insert is unavailable.

questions.prompt: Can a PDF replace a subscriber’s choice automatically?
options: Yes, it is always the required remedy
No, it can be offered in addition
Yes, but only if no more than half are missing
questions.explanation: The agreement allows an optional digital copy alongside either choice.

children.title: Hear the printer’s update
children.instructions: Listen twice. First identify the update, then check the details you need.
children.prompt_text: We can deliver one short run tonight, but I can't promise which routes it will cover until dispatch has sorted the packs. The rest of the run cannot start until Monday. We will know by nine tomorrow which addresses missed the insert.

questions.prompt: When can individual deliveries be identified?
options: Tonight as soon as printing begins
questions.explanation: Dispatch can reconcile the addresses by nine.

questions.prompt: What is known about the remaining copies?
options: They will reach everyone on Monday
Printing them cannot start before Monday
questions.explanation: The printer gives the earliest start, not a delivery promise.

children.title: Tell customer support what to say today
children.prompt_text: Support wants to send personalised messages before dispatch reconciliation.
children.instructions: Say what they can disclose now, when to confirm individual cases, and why they should avoid promising a postal arrival date.
children.goal: Give an actionable response to what you just learned.
children.model_answer: Tell subscribers that part of the print run is delayed. We'll confirm affected addresses by nine tomorrow. The printer cannot restart production until Monday, so we should avoid giving an arrival date for posted copies.

points.label: Do not assume a delivery date

children.title: Write to affected subscribers
children.prompt_text: It is now after the dispatch check. Write to a subscriber whose delivery definitely lacks the insert.
children.instructions: Acknowledge what was missed, give the subscriber two choices, and offer the PDF without taking either choice away.
children.goal: Offer feasible choices without giving some subscribers an unsupported guarantee.
children.model_answer: Your Saturday delivery went out without the print insert we promised. We can send a paper copy by post once the remaining copies are ready, or apply a delivery credit. Please reply with the option you prefer. The remaining print run cannot start before Monday, and we will confirm the postal date once it is available. We can also send a PDF whichever option you choose.
